headline: TRX GOLD'S BUCKREEF DELIVERS +58% — Record Plant Throughput in Q3; 7,426 oz at $4,703/oz Avg Price, Revenue $32.9M, 59% Gross Margin (TSX:TRX)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / TRX Gold Corporation
snippet: TRX Gold Corporation (TSX/NYSE American: TRX) reported Q3 FY2026 results (three months ended May 31, 2026) showing a 58% year-over-year production increase to 7,426 ounces of gold from its Buckreef Gold mine in Tanzania — on record processing plant throughput — at an average realized gold price of $4,703 per ounce. Revenue hit $32.9 million with a 59% gross profit margin and adjusted EBITDA of $20.7 million; over the trailing twelve months the operation generated $115.5 million in revenue and $66.8 million in adjusted EBITDA. A Q3 results conference call was scheduled for July 16 at 9:30 AM EST, and the company reaffirmed that Buckreef's ongoing plant expansion remains on schedule — a clear indicator that Tanzania-based production growth is accelerating without a corresponding rise in unit costs.

headline: MINERS BACK IN FASHION — Gold $4,106 (+0.8%), Silver $59 (+1.6%), Copper $6.16 (+1.8%); Precious Metals Find Footing After Weeks of Iran/Fed Pressure
snippet: Gold, silver and copper all recovered on July 16 as precious and base metals staged a broad-based rebound: gold added 0.8% to $4,106 per ounce, silver gained 1.6% to $59, and US copper climbed 1.8% to $6.16 per pound, driving gold and copper mining equities to lead FTSE 350 risers. The recovery follows weeks of Iran-driven oil inflation, rising Fed rate-hike odds and Treasury yield pressure that compressed gold from a $4,070 high after June CPI data. Analyst Richard Hunter at Interactive Investor called miners "temporarily squarely back in fashion," noting the sector's disconnect from underlying fundamentals: gold remains 27% below January's $5,589 record while central bank demand averages 1,000 tonnes per year and miner cash flows are at historic highs. The July 28–29 FOMC decision now looms as the sector's key short-term binary.

headline: $372M GOLDGROUP-GOLD RESOURCE MERGER CLOSES JULY 17 — Mexico Multi-Mine Producer Born; Don David + Cerro Prieto + Back Forty Michigan Under One Roof
snippet: The US$372 million business combination of Goldgroup Mining Inc. and Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE: GORO) is set to close on or about July 17, 2026, following shareholder approval by both companies on July 2. The merged entity creates a Mexico-focused multi-mine precious metals producer operating the Don David gold mine in Oaxaca, the Cerro Prieto heap-leach gold mine and San Francisco project in Sonora, and the Back Forty polymetallic development project in Michigan — combining Goldgroup's producing asset base with Gold Resource's pipeline and giving the combined company the scale and asset diversification to attract institutional coverage. The closing remains subject to final regulatory conditions.

headline: SCORPIO GOLD NEVADA: 97.99m AT 2.05 g/t Au — Goldwedge Hits 18.19 g/t Over 3.17m, 11.41 g/t Over 4.57m; Phase 2 Pushes Beyond Existing Resource (TSXV:SGN)
snippet: Scorpio Gold Corp. (TSXV: SGN) released results from eighteen step-out holes of the Phase 2 drill program at its Manhattan District Project in Nevada, led by hole 26MN-093 returning 97.99 metres at 2.05 g/t gold from 64.16 metres within the Gold Hill Formation — including high-grade sub-intervals of 18.19 g/t gold over 3.17 metres, 11.41 g/t over 4.57 metres, and 8.98 g/t over 7.32 metres. The Phase 2 program has now completed 102 holes totalling 28,939 metres across the Goldwedge target, with results consistently extending mineralization beyond the current resource model boundary. The historical Manhattan District has hosted multiple Nevada gold mines and remains substantially underexplored at depth.

headline: GALLEON GOLD DRILLS ZONE 9 TO 500m DEPTH — 23.25m AT 2.03 g/t Au Incl. 6.01 g/t; Down-Plunge Extension Vectors Toward Historic West Deep (TSXV:GGO)
snippet: Galleon Gold Corp. (TSXV: GGO) confirmed that 2026 drilling has traced Zone #9 mineralization at its West Cache Gold Project near Timmins, Ontario to a vertical depth of 500 metres, extending 360 metres down-plunge from the planned bulk sample stopes. Highlights include hole WC-26-238 returning 2.03 g/t gold over 23.25 metres (including 6.01 g/t over 4.05 metres) positioned 60 metres below a prior hole that hit 16.07 g/t over 9.25 metres, and WC-26-240 returning 2.61 g/t over 12.0 metres approximately 200 metres below the planned stopes. The down-plunge trend vectors directly toward the West Deep zone discovered in 2010 — if connectivity is confirmed, the combined Zone 9–West Deep corridor would represent a substantially larger mineralized system than either zone alone, with direct implications for West Cache's resource base and future mine planning.

headline: WALLBRIDGE MARTINIERE CONFIRMS BUG LAKE IS GROWING — All 6 Phase 1 Holes Hit Gold-Bearing Structures; Peak 4.34 g/t Over 10m; Phase 2 Delayed by Forest Fires (TSX:WM)
snippet: Wallbridge Mining Company (TSX: WM) released the final four holes of Phase 1 drilling at its 100%-owned Martiniere gold project in Quebec, confirming that all six Phase 1 holes — totalling 4,108 metres along the Bug Lake deformation corridor — intersected multiple gold-bearing structures. Highlighted intervals include 4.34 g/t gold over 10.0 metres and 2.63 g/t gold over 9.8 metres within broader shear-hosted zones. Martiniere lies 30 km west of Wallbridge's flagship Fenelon project and 45 km east of Agnico Eagle's Detour Lake mine; the Bug Lake corridor hosts the majority of the existing Martiniere resource. Phase 2 drilling, originally set to commence in early July, has been temporarily postponed due to nearby forest fires — a near-term operational risk but one that preserves the program for later in 2026.

headline: GOLDSEEK: MINERS HEADING FOR NEAR-RECORD Q2 — Implied Profits $2,787/oz (+50% YoY); 12th Straight Quarter of Huge YoY Earnings Growth, Sector Still Trades at Historical Discount
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis previewing the upcoming Q2 2026 earnings season argues gold miners will report their second-best quarterly results on record: implied unit profits of approximately $2,787 per ounce — up 50% from Q2 2025's $1,861 — on prevailing high gold prices and stable AISC, making this the 12th consecutive quarter of large year-over-year earnings growth. Only Q1 2026's $3,129 per ounce implied profit was higher. Despite this performance, GDX-level mining equities continue to trade at historical valuation discounts, a divergence the analysis frames as a compelling structural opportunity — forced selling during the current correction is setting up an entry point that has historically led to significant re-rating when sentiment shifts.

headline: GOLDSILVER.COM: FED IS SPLIT 9 TO 8 — Gold's Post-FOMC Slide Reversed by July 14 CPI; July 29 FOMC Now the Decisive Binary for Metals
snippet: GoldSilver.com's post-FOMC analysis shows the July 8 Fed minutes revealed a deeply divided committee — nine of eighteen projection participants expect at least one rate hike before year-end, eight project no change — with Chair Kevin Warsh conspicuously withholding his own dot plot projection, the first Fed chair to do so in 14 years. Gold fell to $4,075 and silver to $58.27 on the day of release, but June CPI's 3.5% print on July 14 — sharply below May's 4.2% — reversed both declines, resetting rate-hike odds and reopening the bull case. The article argues the Fed's structural division means the July 28–29 FOMC decision is now the single most important catalyst for gold and silver direction in H2 2026: a hold keeps the rally alive; a hike or renewed hawkish rhetoric re-tests the $4,000 floor.

headline: GREENLAND PLAY LIVE: CRML, UUUU, USAR ADVANCE AS TRUMP REVIVES ARCTIC AMBITIONS AT NATO — Critical Metals Holds 92.5% of Tanbreez, One of World's Largest Heavy REE Deposits
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML), Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU), USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR), REalloys (ALOY), and Greenland Energy Company (GLND) all gained as President Trump renewed his call for U.S. control of Greenland during the NATO summit in Ankara, citing rare earth and Arctic security imperatives. The remarks refocused investor attention on CRML's 92.5% stake in the Tanbreez project in southern Greenland — one of the world's largest undeveloped deposits of heavy rare earth elements used in permanent magnets, EVs, and defense systems — where an ongoing 10,000-metre drill program is targeting resource expansion. China currently controls approximately 70% of global rare earth output and 90% of processing capacity, and has separately added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export control list, compressing the Western supply chain and amplifying the strategic premium on non-Chinese projects.

headline: KITCO GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS Q2 BEATS BY 31% — Vares Mine Shutdown Done in 7 Days vs 20 Planned; Operational Outperformance Sets Up Sector Premium Case (TSX:DPM)
snippet: Kitco's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlights DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) as a standout performer after Q2 2026 gold production of 61,212 ounces exceeded analyst estimates by 31%, driven primarily by Vares in Bosnia where the planned 20-day plant shutdown was completed in just 7 days — a meaningful operational efficiency signal. The Chelopech mine in Bulgaria also posted higher gold and silver grades quarter-over-quarter. The SWOT framing argues DPM's consistent ability to beat operational guidance, combined with gold averaging above $4,700 per ounce through most of Q2 and the sector still trading at a 19% discount to net asset values, creates a specific company-level premium case beyond the general miner value argument. DPM also produced 6.4 million pounds of copper in Q2, providing an additional commodity diversification lever.
